outcome: Weight of larger neonate in twins
cohort: 66 subjects with triplet pregnancies containing monochorionic (MC) twins and an MC singleton who underwent selective reduction
finding: Reducing dichorionic triplet pregnancies to DCDA twins resulted in better pregnancy outcomes, including lower rates of early miscarriage, cesarean section, and late premature delivery, compared to reduction to MCDA twins.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate was significantly lower in the group reduced to DCDA twins (81.6%) compared to the group reduced to MCDA twins (100%).
birth_weight: Total neonatal weight, weight of twins, and weight of the larger neonate in twins were all significantly higher in the group reduced to DCDA twins.
